newsitem.title: UK: British trade deficit narrows in May.
newsitem.headline: British trade deficit narrows in May.

text.p: Britain's global trade deficit narrowed to 508 million pounds ($851.2 million) in May from 989 million the previous month as exports and imports both fell, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday.
Partial figures for June showed Britain had a deficit with countries outside the European Union of 713 million pounds, up from 584 million in May.
The ONS said there was no certain evidence that the strength of the pound, which has surged over 25 percent against major currencies since last year, was having an impact on trade.

"Overall the numbers seem slightly better than the markets had been anticipating," said Andrew Cates, an economist at UBS. "Exports are holding up surprisingly well given the strength of sterling. Equally, there seems to be little evidence that import penetration is rising."
However, James McKay, an economist at Paine Webber, said export volumes were likely to fall and import volumes to rise in the coming months.
"Sterling is certainly starting to take its toll. I don't think we've seen much of an impact yet, I think it's going to get a lot worse later in the year," he said. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
